summary: Lockfile-only change to the nested Cargo workspace at packages/eql: reqwest 0.13.3 -> 0.13.4, which moves hickory-resolver/hickory-proto 0.25.2 -> 0.26.3 (adds hickory-net, system-configuration, prefix-trie, ndk-context; drops enum-as-inner) and re-resolves several Windows-only windows-sys edges to older versions. No Cargo.toml changes. In this workspace reqwest is reachable only through cipherstash-client and stack-auth, which are dependencies of the unpublished eql_tests SQLx harness (publish = false). The published eql-bindings crate and the eql-codegen binary that builds the shipped SQL bundle do not depend on any changed crate, and a lockfile does not travel with a published library crate. The blast radius is therefore the EQL test/fixture harness in CI; any failure would be a loud build or test failure rather than a silent customer-facing one. Impact low; ready for normal review once the test-eql workflow (which path-filters on packages/eql/Cargo.lock) is green.

behaviour_changes.description: The eql_tests harness's HTTP client (reqwest, via cipherstash-client and stack-auth) now resolves DNS through hickory-resolver 0.26.3 instead of 0.25.2. 0.26 splits networking into a new hickory-net crate and adds platform system-configuration reading (macOS) and Android context; on Linux resolv.conf is still read via resolv-conf.

Windows-only windows-sys dependency edges for errno, rustix, quinn-udp, rustls-platform-verifier, tempfile and winapi-util are re-resolved to older windows-sys versions (0.59.0 / 0.48.0) without those crates' versions changing. Only compiled for Windows targets.
Per the commit message, the bump remediates hickory advisories GHSA-q2qq-hmj6-3wpp and GHSA-3v94-mw7p-v465 for this lockfile. Whether 0.26.3 fixes them could not be checked offline.

failure_scenarios.title: hickory 0.26 resolver change breaks the EQL test harness build or its ZeroKMS calls in CI
failure_scenarios.trigger: The eql_tests crate is compiled, or the e2e / fixture-generation suites run, with the new reqwest 0.13.4 + hickory 0.26.3 resolution.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: reqwest uses hickory-resolver for DNS in this graph (E-2). The 0.25 -> 0.26 move restructures the resolver (new hickory-net crate, new system-configuration dependency) and bumps rand to 0.10. A compile incompatibility or a changed resolver configuration on the CI runner would surface as a build error or as DNS/connection failures reaching ZeroKMS from cipherstash-client.
failure_scenarios.consequence: EQL SQLx/e2e CI jobs fail or fixture regeneration cannot reach ZeroKMS. Loud and confined to CI and developer tooling; no published artefact embeds this graph.
